Nia (CS): dropping a 60s pocket runbook for warmup/prefill + rep script — focused on accounts with renewal risk. Keep this in ticket top-lines.
Omar (CS Ops): yes — we need a 3-question decision check and two ticket fields.
Linh (Eng): runtime-safe defaults (copyable):
Linh (Eng): ```yaml
warmup:
  enabled: true
  window_mins: 30
  target_concurrency: 2
cache:
  edge_ttl_s: 45
  kv_ttl_min: 15
batching:
  max_batch_tokens: 1024
  hold_ms: 25
streaming:
  prefer: true
  fallback: single_shot
  partial_timeout_ms: 1200
```
Marco (SRE): add lightweight alerts: probe every 3m; page if p95 > 350ms for 10m or error_rate > 1.5%. Log warmup token usage and tag ticket when >0.5% monthly budget.
Nia (CS): decision check (yes/no x3): 1) chat-like UX? 2) expect >30 first-24h sessions? 3) customer ok with small warmup spend? If >=2 yes -> recommend warmup.
Omar (CS Ops): ticket fields: `warmup_consent: yes/no`, `warmup_notes` (free text). Reps capture objections (cost/privacy) and next steps.
Nia (CS): rep email blurb: "Subject: Short warmup before go-live — Hi <Name>, we plan a brief warmup to improve first-hour latency and UX. It warms a small pool and caches examples for ~1h. No action required — reply to opt out. Thanks, <rep>"
Linh (Eng): ops curl (ops-only):
Linh (Eng): ```bash
curl -X POST https://internal.redwood/v1/warmup -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" -d '{"tenant_id":"T-007","steps":6,"mode":"staggered"}'
```
Marco (SRE): staged demo play: start small warm_pool 20m, ramp concurrency +1 every 10m, watch p95; if p95 spikes, reduce batch hold_ms or pause further ramps. If fallback_count >5 in 1h, open incident.
Nia (CS): renewal trigger (simple): <4 meaningful sessions in 24h AND p95 >250ms for >12h -> flag CS. If flagged twice in 7 days -> schedule health call.
prep-bot: saved pocket runbook draft to Drive: https://drive.redwood/warmup/pocket-1799998881 (owner: Nia)
